chapter_title: The Parliamentary System: Legislature and Executive
root_topic: The Parliamentary System: Legislature and Executive

branches.theme: 6.1 Bicameral Legislature: Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha

details: Parliament comprises the President of India and two houses: Lok Sabha (House of the People) and Rajya Sabha (Council of States).
Lok Sabha directly represents citizens (543 seats, 5-year term); Rajya Sabha represents states indirectly (245 seats, permanent body).
evidence_or_examples: Lok Sabha dissolved every 5 years or sooner; 1/3rd of Rajya Sabha members retire every 2 years.
sub_branches.tooltip_popover: Core concept: Bicameral Structure of Union Parliament. Key terms: Bicameralism, Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, President of India

details: Propose Bill → First Reading → Second Reading (clause-by-clause scrutiny) → Third Reading → Passing in House 1 → House 2 → Presidential Assent → Act.
Money Bills deal strictly with taxation and expenditure; can only be introduced in Lok Sabha.
evidence_or_examples: Rajya Sabha has 14 days to review Money Bills before they are automatically deemed passed.
sub_branches.tooltip_popover: Core concept: Legislative Lawmaking Process. Key terms: Bill to Act, Money Bill, Presidential Assent, Consolidated Fund

details: Executive (Prime Minister & Council of Ministers) remains directly answerable to the elected Lok Sabha.
Oversight tools include Question Hour, Zero Hour, Parliamentary Standing Committees, and No-Confidence Motions.
evidence_or_examples: Question Hour allowing MPs to ask starred questions demanding oral answers from ministers.
Departmentally Related Standing Committees scrutinizing ministry demands for grants.
sub_branches.tooltip_popover: Core concept: Executive Oversight and Accountability Mechanisms. Key terms: Question Hour, Zero Hour, Standing Committees, No-Confidence Motion, Ministerial Accountability

hotspots.label: Bicameral Structure (Lok Sabha & Rajya Sabha)
hotspots.popover_description: Lok Sabha directly represents citizens (543 seats, 5-yr term); Rajya Sabha represents states indirectly (245 seats, permanent body).

hotspots.label: Lawmaking Process (Bill to Act)
hotspots.popover_description: Bill passes 3 readings in House 1, undergoes committee scrutiny, passes House 2, and receives Presidential Assent to become an Act.

hotspots.label: Executive Oversight (Question Hour & Committees)
hotspots.popover_description: MPs question ministers during Question Hour, review budgets in Standing Committees, and can move a No-Confidence Motion.
